novel_features.name: Retraction check
novel_features.description: Tell whether a paper (by DOI or PMID) has been retracted, when, why, and where the notice is.
novel_features.rationale: Crossref embeds Retraction Watch update records; we parse update-to/update-by plus the RETRACTED title signal into one structured verdict no raw API call returns.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Agents citing a paper should verify it is not retracted before relying on it.

novel_features.name: Bibliography scan
novel_features.description: Batch-check a reading list or .bib file and flag every retracted entry.
novel_features.rationale: Reuses the batch-file line pattern (skip blank/# lines) and fans out DOI/PMID lookups against Crossref with a single command.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Catches retracted citations across a whole manuscript or literature review at once.

novel_features.name: Superseding research
novel_features.description: For a retracted or older paper, find related more-recent research on the same topic, ranked by citation count.
novel_features.rationale: Joins Crossref retraction/date context with OpenAlex citation-ranked related works published after the original — a cross-source view no single API provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When a paper is retracted, the agent still needs the current best evidence on the topic.

novel_features.name: Retraction watch
novel_features.description: Monitor a topic or reading list for newly-announced retractions since the last run.
novel_features.rationale: Persists a baseline of seen retraction notices and diffs on each run, using the snapshot/first-run-baseline pattern.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Surfaces new retractions in a field or personal library without re-reading everything.

narrative.headline: Check whether a paper is retracted, why, and what the current research says now — keyless, over Crossref and OpenAlex.
narrative.value_prop: Retraction Checker turns Crossref's embedded Retraction Watch data into a one-shot verdict: is this DOI or PMID retracted, when, why, and where is the notice. It batch-scans reading lists and .bib files, finds citation-ranked superseding research via OpenAlex, and watches a topic or library for newly-announced retractions. Fully keyless.

quickstart.comment: Confirm the CLI and Crossref reachability before checking papers
Check a single DOI for retraction status
Flag retracted entries across a bibliography

troubleshoots.fix: Pass --mailto you@example.com to join the polite pool for better limits
PMIDs are resolved to DOIs first; some records have no DOI and cannot be checked via Crossref

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent or researcher needs to verify that a cited paper has not been retracted, audit a bibliography for retracted references, or find current research that supersedes a retracted study. It is the right choice for citation-integrity checks in literature reviews and RAG pipelines.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to fetch full-text papers or PDFs
Do not use it for general scholarly search unrelated to retraction — use scientific-consensus for consensus and evidence analytics

recipes.title: Check a DOI
recipes.explanation: Returns retraction status, date, reason source, and notice reference for one paper.

recipes.title: Audit a bibliography
recipes.explanation: Scans one DOI/PMID per line and returns only the key retraction fields for each entry.

recipes.title: Find superseding work
recipes.explanation: Lists more-recent related papers ranked by citations, published after the retracted paper.

recipes.title: Watch a field
recipes.explanation: Baselines retraction notices for a topic and reports new ones on later runs.
